scope: Deuteronomy 1–6, all 219 public verses. Prior revisions remain unchanged.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public Deuteronomy 1–6 align directly with all 219 corresponding Hebrew records. Each original XML record is hashed in full.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Retains the full geographical frame and collective audience while making the opening a complete English sentence.
verses.before: These are the words that Moses spoke to all Israel beyond the Jordan, in the wilderness, in the Arabah opposite Suph, between Paran and Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth, and Di-Zahab.
verses.after: These are the words Moses spoke to all Israel beyond the Jordan, in the wilderness of the Arabah opposite Suph, between Paran, Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth, and Dizahab.
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the words that Moses spoke to all Israel beyond the Jordan, in the wilderness, in the Arabah opposite Suph, between Paran and Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth, and Di-Zahab.

verses.rationale: Keeps the eleven-day distance and specified route as the narrator's striking measure of the journey.
verses.before: It is eleven days from Horeb by the way of Mount Seir to Kadesh-Barnea.
verses.after: It is an eleven-day journey from Horeb to Kadesh-barnea by the Mount Seir route.
verses.tsw_comparator: It is eleven days from Horeb by the way of Mount Seir to Kadesh-Barnea.

verses.rationale: Preserves all three date components and Moses' role as the commissioned speaker.
verses.before: In the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, Moses spoke to the children of Israel according to all that the LORD had commanded him concerning them.
verses.after: In the fortieth year, on the first day of the eleventh month, Moses told the Israelites everything the LORD had commanded him to tell them.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, Moses spoke to the children of Israel according to all that the LORD had commanded him concerning them.

verses.rationale: Takes at Edrei as the location of Og's defeat; a note identifies the compressed geographical syntax.
verses.before: This was after he had struck Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, and Og king of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth at Edrei.
verses.after: This was after he had defeated Sihon, the Amorite king who lived in Heshbon, and Og, the king of Bashan who lived in Ashtaroth, whom he defeated at Edrei.
verses.tsw_comparator: This was after he had struck Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, and Og king of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth at Edrei.

verses.rationale: Renders torah as instruction here and preserves the shift from narrative frame to Moses' explanation.
verses.before: Beyond the Jordan in the land of Moab, Moses began to explain this instruction, saying:
verses.after: There in Moab, beyond the Jordan, Moses began to explain this instruction. He said,
verses.tsw_comparator: Beyond the Jordan in the land of Moab, Moses began to explain this instruction, saying:

verses.rationale: Keeps the shared our God and the command's time emphasis at the beginning of the remembered speech.
verses.before: “The LORD our God spoke to us at Horeb, saying, ‘You have stayed long enough at this mountain.
verses.after: “The LORD our God said to us at Horeb, ‘You have stayed at this mountain long enough.
verses.tsw_comparator: “The LORD our God spoke to us at Horeb, saying, ‘You have stayed long enough at this mountain.

verses.rationale: Preserves the sequence of regions and the far boundary rather than compressing the land list.
verses.before: Turn and set out. Go to the hill country of the Amorites and to all their neighbors in the Arabah, the hill country, the foothills, the Negev, and the seacoast, the land of the Canaanites and Lebanon, as far as the great river, the Euphrates River.
verses.after: Turn and set out. Go to the hill country of the Amorites and all its neighboring regions—the Arabah, the hill country, the lowlands, the Negev, and the coast—the land of the Canaanites and Lebanon, as far as the great river, the Euphrates.
verses.tsw_comparator: Turn and set out. Go to the hill country of the Amorites and to all their neighbors in the Arabah, the hill country, the foothills, the Negev, and the seacoast, the land of the Canaanites and Lebanon, as far as the great river, the Euphrates River.

verses.rationale: Retains the see imperative, possession language, named ancestors, and continuing descendants.
verses.before: See, I have set the land before you. Go in and possess the land that the LORD swore to your ancestors, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, to give to them and to their offspring after them.’
verses.after: See, I have placed the land before you. Go in and take possession of the land the LORD swore to give your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and their descendants after them.’
verses.tsw_comparator: See, I have set the land before you. Go in and possess the land that the LORD swore to your ancestors, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, to give to them and to their offspring after them.’

verses.rationale: Keeps carry as the governing burden image rather than replacing it with generic administration.
verses.before: “At that time I said to you, ‘I am not able to carry you by myself.
verses.after: At that time I told you, ‘I cannot carry you by myself.
verses.tsw_comparator: “At that time I said to you, ‘I am not able to carry you by myself.

verses.rationale: Preserves the present-day comparison and repeated abundance language.
verses.before: The LORD your God has multiplied you, and look, today you are as numerous as the stars of the heavens.
verses.after: The LORD your God has made you numerous. Today you are as numerous as the stars in the sky.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD your God has multiplied you, and look, today you are as numerous as the stars of the heavens.

verses.rationale: Retains the precise thousandfold wish and its connection to the ancestral promise.
verses.before: May the LORD, the God of your ancestors, add to you a thousand times as many as you are and bless you, as he has spoken concerning you.
verses.after: May the LORD, the God of your fathers, make you a thousand times as numerous and bless you as he promised you!
verses.tsw_comparator: May the LORD, the God of your ancestors, add to you a thousand times as many as you are and bless you, as he has spoken concerning you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the three distinct burdens and the rhetorical question.
verses.before: How can I carry by myself your burden, your load, and your disputes?
verses.after: But how can I carry your troubles, your burdens, and your disputes alone?
verses.tsw_comparator: How can I carry by myself your burden, your load, and your disputes?

verses.rationale: Preserves the male appointees, three qualifications, tribal selection, and Moses' appointment.
verses.before: Choose for yourselves wise, understanding, and experienced men from your tribes, and I will appoint them as your heads.’
verses.after: Choose wise, discerning, respected men from your tribes, and I will appoint them as your leaders.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Choose for yourselves wise, understanding, and experienced men from your tribes, and I will appoint them as your heads.’

verses.rationale: Keeps the people's explicit agreement as direct speech.
verses.before: You answered me and said, ‘The thing you have spoken is good for us to do.’
verses.after: You answered me, ‘What you propose is good.’
verses.tsw_comparator: You answered me and said, ‘The thing you have spoken is good for us to do.’

verses.rationale: Retains the full descending numerical structure and the additional officers.
verses.before: So I took the heads of your tribes, wise and experienced men, and appointed them as heads over you: leaders of thousands, leaders of hundreds, leaders of fifties, leaders of tens, and officers for your tribes.
verses.after: So I took your tribal leaders, wise and respected men, and appointed them over you: commanders of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens, and officers for your tribes.
verses.tsw_comparator: So I took the heads of your tribes, wise and experienced men, and appointed them as heads over you: leaders of thousands, leaders of hundreds, leaders of fifties, leaders of tens, and officers for your tribes.

verses.rationale: Makes the hearing function explicit while preserving brother language and the foreigner's inclusion.
verses.before: I commanded your judges at that time, saying, ‘Hear the cases between your brothers and judge righteously between a man and his brother or the resident alien who is with him.
verses.after: At that time I instructed your judges, ‘Hear the disputes between your brothers. Judge fairly between a man and his brother or the resident foreigner living with him.
verses.tsw_comparator: I commanded your judges at that time, saying, ‘Hear the cases between your brothers and judge righteously between a man and his brother or the resident alien who is with him.

verses.rationale: Unfolds the facial-partiality idiom and retains equal hearing, divine accountability, and referral.
verses.before: You will not show partiality in judgment. You will hear the small and the great alike. You will not fear the face of any man, for the judgment belongs to God. The case that is too difficult for you, bring to me, and I will hear it.’
verses.after: Show no favoritism in judgment. Hear the small and the great alike. Do not be afraid of anyone, because judgment belongs to God. Bring me any case too difficult for you, and I will hear it.’
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not show partiality in judgment. You shall hear the small and the great alike. You shall not fear the face of any man, for the judgment belongs to God. The case that is too difficult for you, bring to me, and I will hear it.’

verses.rationale: Preserves the comprehensive closing statement and repeated time marker.
verses.before: I commanded you at that time all the things that you were to do.
verses.after: At that time I instructed you about everything you were to do.
verses.tsw_comparator: I commanded you at that time all the things that you were to do.

verses.rationale: Keeps the wilderness' frightening scale and the link between travel and command.
verses.before: “Then we set out from Horeb and went through all that great and fearsome wilderness that you saw, by the way of the hill country of the Amorites, as the LORD our God had commanded us, and we came to Kadesh-Barnea.
verses.after: Then we left Horeb and traveled through that whole vast, terrifying wilderness you saw, on the way to the Amorite hill country, as the LORD our God commanded us. We reached Kadesh-barnea.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Then we set out from Horeb and went through all that great and fearsome wilderness that you saw, by the way of the hill country of the Amorites, as the LORD our God had commanded us, and we came to Kadesh-Barnea.

verses.rationale: Retains both you and us within Moses' collective account of the gift.
verses.before: I said to you, ‘You have come to the hill country of the Amorites, which the LORD our God is giving us.
verses.after: I told you, ‘You have reached the Amorite hill country, which the LORD our God is giving us.
verses.tsw_comparator: I said to you, ‘You have come to the hill country of the Amorites, which the LORD our God is giving us.

verses.rationale: Repeats placed before and possession language and preserves the two prohibitions against fear.
verses.before: See, the LORD your God has set the land before you. Go up, possess it, as the LORD, the God of your ancestors, has spoken to you. Do not fear or be dismayed.’
verses.after: See, the LORD your God has placed the land before you. Go up and take possession, as the LORD, the God of your fathers, told you. Do not be afraid or lose heart.’
verses.tsw_comparator: See, the LORD your God has set the land before you. Go up, possess it, as the LORD, the God of your ancestors, has spoken to you. Do not fear or be dismayed.’

verses.rationale: Retains Moses' attribution of the scouting proposal to the people without harmonizing another account.
verses.before: Then all of you came near to me and said, ‘Let us send men before us, so that they may explore the land for us and bring back word concerning the way by which we should go up and the cities into which we will come.’
verses.after: Then all of you came to me and said, ‘Let us send men ahead of us to explore the land and report back on the route we should take and the towns we will reach.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Then all of you came near to me and said, ‘Let us send men before us, so that they may explore the land for us and bring back word concerning the way by which we should go up and the cities into which we will come.’

verses.rationale: Keeps Moses' agreement and both the total and tribal distribution.
verses.before: The matter was good in my eyes, so I took twelve men from among you, one man for each tribe.
verses.after: The proposal seemed good to me, so I chose twelve men from among you, one from each tribe.
verses.tsw_comparator: The matter was good in my eyes, so I took twelve men from among you, one man for each tribe.

verses.rationale: Preserves the ascent, named valley, and scouting action in sequence.
verses.before: They turned and went up into the hill country, came to the Valley of Eshcol, and explored it.
verses.after: They went up into the hill country, reached the Valley of Eshcol, and explored it.
verses.tsw_comparator: They turned and went up into the hill country, came to the Valley of Eshcol, and explored it.

verses.rationale: Retains the fruit as tangible evidence and the positive shared report.
verses.before: They took some of the fruit of the land in their hands and brought it down to us. They brought us back word and said, ‘The land that the LORD our God is giving us is good.’
verses.after: They took some of the land's fruit and brought it down to us. They reported, ‘The land the LORD our God is giving us is good.’
verses.tsw_comparator: They took some of the fruit of the land in their hands and brought it down to us. They brought us back word and said, ‘The land that the LORD our God is giving us is good.’

verses.rationale: Keeps refusal and rebellion as two accusations rather than weakening either.
verses.before: “Yet you would not go up, but rebelled against the mouth of the LORD your God.
verses.after: But you refused to go up. You rebelled against the command of the LORD your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Yet you would not go up, but rebelled against the mouth of the LORD your God.

verses.rationale: Preserves the accusation of divine hatred as the people's speech, not the narrator's judgment.
verses.before: You murmured in your tents and said, ‘Because the LORD hates us, he brought us out from the land of Egypt to give us into the hand of the Amorites to destroy us.
verses.after: You grumbled in your tents and said, ‘The LORD hates us! That is why he brought us out of Egypt—to hand us over to the Amorites and destroy us.
verses.tsw_comparator: You murmured in your tents and said, ‘Because the LORD hates us, he brought us out from the land of Egypt to give us into the hand of the Amorites to destroy us.

verses.rationale: Retains the melting-heart image, heightened fortifications, and the reported Anakim without literalizing the hyperbole.
verses.before: Where are we going up? Our brothers have made our hearts melt, saying, “The people are greater and taller than we are; the cities are great and fortified to the heavens. Moreover, we saw the children of the Anakim there.”’
verses.after: Where can we go? Our brothers have made our hearts melt by saying, “The people are bigger and taller than we are. Their towns are large, fortified up to the heavens. We even saw Anakim there.”’
verses.tsw_comparator: Where are we going up? Our brothers have made our hearts melt, saying, “The people are greater and taller than we are; the cities are great and fortified to the heavens. Moreover, we saw the children of the Anakim there.”’

verses.rationale: Preserves the paired fear prohibitions and their immediate object.
verses.before: Then I said to you, ‘Do not be terrified and do not fear them.
verses.after: Then I told you, ‘Do not dread them. Do not be afraid of them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I said to you, ‘Do not be terrified and do not fear them.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine advance and fighting, with the comparison continuing into the next verse.
verses.before: The LORD your God, who goes before you, he himself will fight for you, just as he did for you in Egypt before your eyes,
verses.after: The LORD your God goes ahead of you. He will fight for you, just as you saw him do for you in Egypt,
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD your God, who goes before you, he himself will fight for you, just as he did for you in Egypt before your eyes,

verses.rationale: Retains the specifically male father-son image and its connection to the earlier carrying burden.
verses.before: and in the wilderness, where you saw how the LORD your God carried you, as a man carries his son, in all the way that you went until you came to this place.
verses.after: and in the wilderness. There you saw how the LORD your God carried you, as a man carries his son, all the way you traveled until you reached this place.’
verses.tsw_comparator: and in the wilderness, where you saw how the LORD your God carried you, as a man carries his son, in all the way that you went until you came to this place.

verses.rationale: Preserves the indictment of distrust and lets its description continue across verse labels.
verses.before: Yet in this matter you did not trust the LORD your God,
verses.after: Yet even with all this, you did not trust the LORD your God,
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet in this matter you did not trust the LORD your God,

verses.rationale: Keeps God's scouting role, camping purpose, and separate night/day guidance.
verses.before: who went before you on the way to seek out a place for you to camp, in fire by night to show you the way you should go, and in the cloud by day.
verses.after: who went ahead of you on the road to find a place for you to camp. He showed you the way to go, with fire by night and a cloud by day.
verses.tsw_comparator: who went before you on the way to seek out a place for you to camp, in fire by night to show you the way you should go, and in the cloud by day.

verses.rationale: Preserves the hearing, anger, and oath sequence without obscuring the oath's introduction.
verses.before: “The LORD heard the sound of your words and became angry and swore, saying,
verses.after: When the LORD heard what you said, he became angry and swore,
verses.tsw_comparator: “The LORD heard the sound of your words and became angry and swore, saying,

verses.rationale: Retains evil generation versus good land and the oath's negative force.
verses.before: ‘Not one of these men of this evil generation will see the good land that I swore to give to your ancestors,
verses.after: ‘Not one of these men, this evil generation, will see the good land I swore to give your fathers,
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘Not one of these men of this evil generation shall see the good land that I swore to give to your ancestors,

verses.rationale: Preserves the named exception, descendants' share, walked land, and full allegiance.
verses.before: except Caleb son of Jephunneh. He will see it, and to him and to his sons I will give the land on which he has walked, because he fully followed the LORD.’
verses.after: except Caleb son of Jephunneh. He will see it. I will give him and his sons the land he walked on, because he followed the LORD wholeheartedly.’
verses.tsw_comparator: except Caleb son of Jephunneh. He shall see it, and to him and to his sons I will give the land on which he has walked, because he fully followed the LORD.’

verses.rationale: Leaves Moses' because of you claim intact in his own voice without replacing it with Numbers' explanation.
verses.before: The LORD was angry with me also because of you, saying, ‘You also will not enter there.
verses.after: The LORD was angry with me too because of you. He said, ‘You will not enter it either.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD was angry with me also because of you, saying, ‘You also shall not enter there.

verses.rationale: Renders standing before as service and preserves Joshua's role in Israel's inheritance.
verses.before: Joshua son of Nun, who stands before you, he will enter there. Strengthen him, for he will cause Israel to inherit it.
verses.after: Joshua son of Nun, who serves you, will enter it. Strengthen him, because he will lead Israel into its inheritance.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua son of Nun, who stands before you, he shall enter there. Strengthen him, for he shall cause Israel to inherit it.

verses.rationale: Keeps the threatened children, their stated lack of moral knowledge, and the emphatic reversal of inheritance.
verses.before: And your little children, whom you said would become plunder, and your children who today do not know good or evil, they will enter there. To them I will give it, and they will possess it.
verses.after: Your little ones, whom you said would become plunder, and your children, who today do not know good from evil—they will enter it. I will give it to them, and they will take possession of it.
verses.tsw_comparator: And your little children, whom you said would become plunder, and your children who today do not know good or evil, they shall enter there. To them I will give it, and they shall possess it.

verses.rationale: Retains the contrast between children and the addressed generation and the route designation.
verses.before: But as for you, turn and set out for the wilderness by the way of the Sea of Reeds.’
verses.after: As for you, turn back and set out into the wilderness by the Sea of Reeds route.’
verses.tsw_comparator: But as for you, turn and set out for the wilderness by the way of the Sea of Reeds.’

verses.rationale: Preserves the confession and renewed claim of obedience; renders the difficult readiness verb as confident ease with a note.
verses.before: “Then you answered and said to me, ‘We have sinned against the LORD. We ourselves will go up and fight, according to all that the LORD our God commanded us.’ So each man strapped on his weapons of war, and you thought it easy to go up into the hill country.
verses.after: Then you answered me, ‘We have sinned against the LORD. We will go up and fight, just as the LORD our God commanded us.’ Each of you strapped on his weapons, thinking it would be easy to go up into the hill country.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Then you answered and said to me, ‘We have sinned against the LORD. We ourselves will go up and fight, according to all that the LORD our God commanded us.’ So each man strapped on his weapons of war, and you thought it easy to go up into the hill country.

verses.rationale: Keeps the prohibition, absence, and threatened defeat as the message Moses must relay.
verses.before: But the LORD said to me, ‘Say to them: Do not go up and do not fight, for I am not in your midst, lest you be struck down before your enemies.’
verses.after: But the LORD told me, ‘Tell them not to go up or fight, because I will not be among them. Otherwise they will be defeated by their enemies.’
verses.tsw_comparator: But the LORD said to me, ‘Say to them: Do not go up and do not fight, for I am not in your midst, lest you be struck down before your enemies.’

verses.rationale: Retains both disobedience and presumptuous advance rather than describing merely a tactical mistake.
verses.before: So I spoke to you, but you did not listen. You rebelled against the mouth of the LORD and acted presumptuously and went up into the hill country.
verses.after: I told you, but you would not listen. You rebelled against the LORD's command and arrogantly went up into the hill country.
verses.tsw_comparator: So I spoke to you, but you did not listen. You rebelled against the mouth of the LORD and acted presumptuously and went up into the hill country.

verses.rationale: Keeps the bee simile and the full geographical extent of the rout.
verses.before: Then the Amorites who lived in that hill country came out against you and chased you as bees do. They struck you down in Seir as far as Hormah.
verses.after: The Amorites who lived in that hill country came out against you. They chased you like bees and crushed you in Seir, as far as Hormah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the Amorites who lived in that hill country came out against you and chased you as bees do. They struck you down in Seir as far as Hormah.

verses.rationale: Preserves both expressions of refused hearing despite the people's tears.
verses.before: You returned and wept before the LORD, but the LORD did not listen to your voice or give ear to you.
verses.after: You came back and wept before the LORD, but the LORD would not listen to your voice or give you a hearing.
verses.tsw_comparator: You returned and wept before the LORD, but the LORD did not listen to your voice or give ear to you.

verses.rationale: Retains the deliberately indefinite repeated duration instead of inventing a length of stay.
verses.before: So you remained at Kadesh many days, according to the days that you remained there.
verses.after: So you stayed at Kadesh for many days—all those days you spent there.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So you remained at Kadesh many days, according to the days that you remained there.

verses.rationale: Preserves the return route, Moses' instruction, and the prolonged movement around Seir.
verses.before: “Then we turned and set out for the wilderness by the way of the Sea of Reeds, as the LORD had spoken to me, and we went around Mount Seir many days.
verses.after: “Then we turned and set out into the wilderness by the Sea of Reeds route, as the LORD had told me. For many days we traveled around Mount Seir.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Then we turned and set out for the wilderness by the way of the Sea of Reeds, as the LORD had spoken to me, and we went around Mount Seir many days.

verses.rationale: Keeps the divine speech introduction joined to its following command.
verses.before: Then the LORD spoke to me, saying,
verses.after: Then the LORD said to me,
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD spoke to me, saying,

verses.rationale: Echoes the earlier long-enough command while retaining the new direction.
verses.before: ‘You have gone around this mountain long enough. Turn northward.
verses.after: ‘You have traveled around this mountain long enough. Turn north.
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘You have gone around this mountain long enough. Turn northward.

verses.rationale: Keeps Esau's kinship, the inhabitants' fear, and the resulting caution.
verses.before: Command the people, saying, “You are about to pass through the territory of your brothers, the children of Esau who live in Seir. They will be afraid of you, so be very careful.
verses.after: Give the people this command: You are about to pass through the territory of your brothers, the descendants of Esau, who live in Seir. They will be afraid of you, so be very careful.
verses.tsw_comparator: Command the people, saying, “You are about to pass through the territory of your brothers, the children of Esau who live in Seir. They will be afraid of you, so be very careful.

verses.rationale: Preserves the foot-sole image and God's grant to another related people.
verses.before: Do not contend with them, for I will not give you any of their land, not even enough for the sole of a foot to tread, because I have given Mount Seir to Esau as a possession.
verses.after: Do not provoke them to conflict. I will not give you any of their land, not even enough for the sole of a foot, because I have given Mount Seir to Esau as his possession.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not contend with them, for I will not give you any of their land, not even enough for the sole of a foot to tread, because I have given Mount Seir to Esau as a possession.

verses.rationale: Retains the separate purchase requirements and repeated payment rather than implying free supplies.
verses.before: You will buy food from them with silver so that you may eat, and you will also purchase water from them with silver so that you may drink.
verses.after: Pay them silver for the food you eat, and pay them silver for the water you drink.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall buy food from them with silver so that you may eat, and you shall also purchase water from them with silver so that you may drink.

verses.rationale: Keeps work of hands, the forty-year duration, and the assurance of no lack.
verses.before: For the LORD your God has blessed you in all the work of your hands. He knows your walking through this great wilderness. These forty years the LORD your God has been with you; you have lacked nothing.”’
verses.after: For the LORD your God has blessed all the work of your hands. He has watched over your journey through this vast wilderness. These forty years the LORD your God has been with you, and you have lacked nothing.’
verses.tsw_comparator: For the LORD your God has blessed you in all the work of your hands. He knows your walking through this great wilderness. These forty years the LORD your God has been with you; you have lacked nothing.”’

verses.rationale: Preserves both named route points and the turn toward Moab without removing repeated kinship language.
verses.before: “So we passed by our brothers, the children of Esau who live in Seir, away from the way of the Arabah, from Elath and Ezion-Geber. Then we turned and passed by the way of the wilderness of Moab.
verses.after: So we passed by our brothers, the descendants of Esau who live in Seir, leaving the Arabah route from Elath and Ezion-geber. We turned and took the route through the wilderness of Moab.
verses.tsw_comparator: “So we passed by our brothers, the children of Esau who live in Seir, away from the way of the Arabah, from Elath and Ezion-Geber. Then we turned and passed by the way of the wilderness of Moab.

verses.rationale: Keeps the double restraint and the divine land grant to Lot's descendants.
verses.before: The LORD said to me, ‘Do not harass Moab and do not contend with them in battle, for I will not give you any of their land as a possession, because I have given Ar to the children of Lot as a possession.’
verses.after: The LORD said to me, ‘Do not harass Moab or provoke them to war. I will not give you any of their land as a possession, because I have given Ar to the descendants of Lot as their possession.’
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to me, ‘Do not harass Moab and do not contend with them in battle, for I will not give you any of their land as a possession, because I have given Ar to the children of Lot as a possession.’

verses.rationale: Preserves the earlier inhabitants and all three descriptions of their scale.
verses.before: The Emim formerly lived there, a people great and numerous and tall as the Anakim.
verses.after: The Emim lived there before—a people great and numerous, as tall as the Anakim.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Emim formerly lived there, a people great and numerous and tall as the Anakim.

verses.rationale: Retains distinct classification and local naming without treating the names as interchangeable everywhere.
verses.before: They also were regarded as Rephaim, like the Anakim, but the Moabites call them Emim.
verses.after: Like the Anakim, they too were counted as Rephaim, but the Moabites called them Emim.
verses.tsw_comparator: They also were regarded as Rephaim, like the Anakim, but the Moabites call them Emim.

verses.rationale: Keeps the retrospective Israel comparison without rewriting its chronology or softening destruction.
verses.before: The Horites also formerly lived in Seir, but the children of Esau dispossessed them and destroyed them from before them and lived in their place, just as Israel did to the land of his possession that the LORD gave to them.
verses.after: The Horites once lived in Seir, but Esau's descendants drove them out, destroyed them, and settled in their place, just as Israel did in the land of its possession that the LORD gave them.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Horites also formerly lived in Seir, but the children of Esau dispossessed them and destroyed them from before them and lived in their place, just as Israel did to the land of his possession that the LORD gave to them.

verses.rationale: Preserves the command and its repeated fulfillment, with speech resumed after the historical aside.
verses.before: “‘Now rise and cross the Wadi Zered.’ So we crossed the Wadi Zered.
verses.after: ‘Now get up and cross the Wadi Zered.’ So we crossed the Wadi Zered.
verses.tsw_comparator: “‘Now rise and cross the Wadi Zered.’ So we crossed the Wadi Zered.

verses.rationale: Retains the exact thirty-eight-year interval, endpoints, and oath-bound loss of the fighting generation.
verses.before: The time that we traveled from Kadesh-Barnea until we crossed the Wadi Zered was thirty-eight years, until all the generation of the men of war had come to an end from the midst of the camp, as the LORD had sworn to them.
verses.after: Thirty-eight years passed between our departure from Kadesh-barnea and our crossing of the Wadi Zered. By then that entire generation of fighting men had died out from the camp, as the LORD had sworn to them.
verses.tsw_comparator: The time that we traveled from Kadesh-Barnea until we crossed the Wadi Zered was thirty-eight years, until all the generation of the men of war had come to an end from the midst of the camp, as the LORD had sworn to them.

verses.rationale: Keeps direct divine agency and the destructive hand image.
verses.before: Indeed, the hand of the LORD was against them to destroy them from the midst of the camp until they came to an end.
verses.after: The LORD's hand was against them too, to wipe them out from the camp until they were gone.
verses.tsw_comparator: Indeed, the hand of the LORD was against them to destroy them from the midst of the camp until they came to an end.

verses.rationale: Lets the temporal clause continue across its verse boundary without inventing a new event.
verses.before: “When all the men of war had finished dying from among the people,
verses.after: When all the fighting men among the people had died,
verses.tsw_comparator: “When all the men of war had finished dying from among the people,

verses.rationale: Preserves the speech introduction as part of the continuing sentence.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to me, saying,
verses.after: the LORD said to me,
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to me, saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps the present-day command and named border locality.
verses.before: ‘Today you are crossing the border of Moab at Ar.
verses.after: ‘Today you are crossing the border of Moab at Ar.
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘Today you are crossing the border of Moab at Ar.

verses.rationale: Preserves a second grant to Lot's descendants and its matching ban on aggression.
verses.before: When you approach opposite the children of Ammon, do not harass them or contend with them, for I will not give you any of the land of the children of Ammon as a possession, because I have given it to the children of Lot as a possession.’
verses.after: When you approach the Ammonites, do not harass them or provoke them to conflict. I will not give you any Ammonite land as a possession, because I have given it to the descendants of Lot as their possession.’
verses.tsw_comparator: When you approach opposite the children of Ammon, do not harass them or contend with them, for I will not give you any of the land of the children of Ammon as a possession, because I have given it to the children of Lot as a possession.’

verses.rationale: Keeps the territorial classification and Ammonite name distinct from the earlier Moabite name.
verses.before: It also is regarded as a land of Rephaim. Rephaim formerly lived in it, but the Ammonites call them Zamzummim,
verses.after: That too is considered a land of Rephaim. Rephaim lived there before, and the Ammonites called them Zamzummim.
verses.tsw_comparator: It also is regarded as a land of Rephaim. Rephaim formerly lived in it, but the Ammonites call them Zamzummim,

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated description and assigns destruction to the LORD as the source does.
verses.before: a people great and numerous and tall as the Anakim. But the LORD destroyed them before the Ammonites, and they dispossessed them and lived in their place,
verses.after: They were a people great and numerous, as tall as the Anakim. But the LORD destroyed them before the Ammonites, who drove them out and settled in their place.
verses.tsw_comparator: a people great and numerous and tall as the Anakim. But the LORD destroyed them before the Ammonites, and they dispossessed them and lived in their place,

verses.rationale: Keeps the comparison with Esau, the replacement sequence, and the narrator's continuing-time marker.
verses.before: just as he did for the children of Esau who live in Seir, when he destroyed the Horites before them, and they dispossessed them and lived in their place to this day.
verses.after: He did the same for Esau's descendants who live in Seir, destroying the Horites before them. They drove them out and settled in their place, where they live to this day.
verses.tsw_comparator: just as he did for the children of Esau who live in Seir, when he destroyed the Horites before them, and they dispossessed them and lived in their place to this day.

verses.rationale: Retains both unfamiliar people names, their place of origin, and the violent replacement.
verses.before: And the Avvim who lived in villages as far as Gaza—the Caphtorim who came out from Caphtor destroyed them and lived in their place.
verses.after: As for the Avvim who lived in villages as far as Gaza, the Caphtorim who came from Caphtor destroyed them and settled in their place.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the Avvim who lived in villages as far as Gaza—the Caphtorim who came out from Caphtor destroyed them and lived in their place.

verses.rationale: Keeps the three movement commands and the transition from protected neighboring lands to commanded battle.
verses.before: “‘Rise, set out, and cross the Wadi Arnon. See, I have given into your hand Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land. Begin to possess it, and contend with him in battle.
verses.after: ‘Get up, set out, and cross the Wadi Arnon. See, I have handed over to you Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land. Begin taking possession, and engage him in battle.
verses.tsw_comparator: “‘Rise, set out, and cross the Wadi Arnon. See, I have given into your hand Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land. Begin to possess it, and contend with him in battle.

verses.rationale: Preserves the expansive horizon and bodily force of the fear language.
verses.before: This day I will begin to put the dread and fear of you upon the peoples under all the heavens, who will hear the report of you and tremble and writhe because of you.’
verses.after: Today I will begin to put dread and fear of you on the peoples everywhere under heaven. When they hear reports of you, they will tremble and writhe in anguish because of you.’
verses.tsw_comparator: This day I will begin to put the dread and fear of you upon the peoples under all the heavens, who will hear the report of you and tremble and writhe because of you.’

verses.rationale: Keeps the peace overture beside the preceding battle command without resolving the narrative tension.
verses.before: “Then I sent messengers from the wilderness of Kedemoth to Sihon king of Heshbon with words of peace, saying,
verses.after: From the wilderness of Kedemoth I sent messengers to Sihon king of Heshbon with words of peace.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Then I sent messengers from the wilderness of Kedemoth to Sihon king of Heshbon with words of peace, saying,

verses.rationale: Retains the first-person collective request and strict route limitation.
verses.before: ‘Let me pass through your land. I will go only by the road; I will not turn aside to the right or to the left.
verses.after: ‘Let me pass through your land. I will stay on the road and turn neither right nor left.
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘Let me pass through your land. I will go only by the road; I will not turn aside to the right or to the left.

verses.rationale: Preserves the separate purchases and on-foot request, continuing into the comparison.
verses.before: You will sell me food for silver so that I may eat, and give me water for silver so that I may drink. Only let me pass through on foot,
verses.after: Sell me food for silver so I can eat, and give me water for silver so I can drink. Only let me pass through on foot,
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall sell me food for silver so that I may eat, and give me water for silver so that I may drink. Only let me pass through on foot,

verses.rationale: Leaves the scope of the comparison with Esau and Moab open rather than harmonizing the passage with Numbers.
verses.before: just as the children of Esau who live in Seir and the Moabites who live in Ar did for me, until I cross the Jordan into the land that the LORD our God is giving us.’
verses.after: as Esau's descendants who live in Seir and the Moabites who live in Ar did for me, until I cross the Jordan into the land the LORD our God is giving us.’
verses.tsw_comparator: just as the children of Esau who live in Seir and the Moabites who live in Ar did for me, until I cross the Jordan into the land that the LORD our God is giving us.’

verses.rationale: Retains both human refusal and explicitly purposive divine hardening without substituting mere permission.
verses.before: Yet Sihon king of Heshbon was not willing to let us pass through him, for the LORD your God hardened his spirit and made his heart stubborn, in order to give him into your hand, as he is this day.
verses.after: But Sihon king of Heshbon would not let us pass through his territory. The LORD your God had hardened his spirit and made his heart unyielding, to hand him over to you, as he has now done.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Sihon king of Heshbon was not willing to let us pass through him, for the LORD your God hardened his spirit and made his heart stubborn, in order to give him into your hand, as he is this day.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated begin language and the link between divine grant and taking possession.
verses.before: “The LORD said to me, ‘See, I have begun to give Sihon and his land before you. Begin to possess, so that you may possess his land.’
verses.after: The LORD said to me, ‘See, I have begun handing Sihon and his land over to you. Begin taking possession, so that his land becomes yours.’
verses.tsw_comparator: “The LORD said to me, ‘See, I have begun to give Sihon and his land before you. Begin to possess, so that you may possess his land.’

verses.rationale: Keeps the entire force and named battlefield.
verses.before: Then Sihon came out against us, he and all his people, for battle at Jahaz.
verses.after: Then Sihon and all his people came out to meet us in battle at Jahaz.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Sihon came out against us, he and all his people, for battle at Jahaz.

verses.rationale: Follows the source's read form his sons rather than the singular written form and records both in the source binding.
verses.before: The LORD our God gave him before us, and we struck him, his sons, and all his people.
verses.after: The LORD our God handed him over to us, and we struck him down, along with his sons and all his people.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD our God gave him before us, and we struck him, his sons, and all his people.

verses.rationale: Preserves the ban term alongside explicit victims and total killing; no euphemistic displacement language.
verses.before: We captured all his cities at that time and devoted every city to destruction—men, women, and little children. We left no survivor.
verses.after: At that time we captured all his towns and devoted every town to destruction—men, women, and little children. We left no survivor.
verses.tsw_comparator: We captured all his cities at that time and devoted every city to destruction—men, women, and little children. We left no survivor.

verses.rationale: Keeps livestock and captured-town spoil as the stated exceptions.
verses.before: Only the livestock we took as plunder for ourselves, along with the spoil of the cities that we captured.
verses.after: We took only the livestock as plunder for ourselves, along with the spoil from the towns we captured.
verses.tsw_comparator: Only the livestock we took as plunder for ourselves, along with the spoil of the cities that we captured.

verses.rationale: Retains the separate town in the wadi and the full extent of the claimed victory.
verses.before: From Aroer, which is on the edge of the Wadi Arnon, and the city that is in the valley, as far as Gilead, there was no city too high for us. The LORD our God gave all before us.
verses.after: From Aroer on the edge of the Wadi Arnon, including the town in the wadi, as far as Gilead, no town was too strong for us. The LORD our God handed them all over to us.
verses.tsw_comparator: From Aroer, which is on the edge of the Wadi Arnon, and the city that is in the valley, as far as Gilead, there was no city too high for us. The LORD our God gave all before us.

verses.rationale: Unfolds the compressed command reference as prohibition in context and retains the excluded boundary areas.
verses.before: Only to the land of the children of Ammon you did not draw near: all the side of the Wadi Jabbok, the cities of the hill country, and wherever the LORD our God had commanded us not to go.
verses.after: But you did not approach Ammonite land—the whole bank of the Wadi Jabbok and the towns of the hill country—anywhere the LORD our God had forbidden you to go.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Only to the land of the children of Ammon you did not draw near: all the side of the Wadi Jabbok, the cities of the hill country, and wherever the LORD our God had commanded us not to go.

verses.rationale: Keeps the travel-to-battle sequence and the named king and battlefield.
verses.before: “Then we turned and went up by the way of Bashan, and Og king of Bashan came out against us, he and all his people, for battle at Edrei.
verses.after: “Then we turned and went up the road to Bashan. Og king of Bashan and all his people came out to meet us in battle at Edrei.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Then we turned and went up by the way of Bashan, and Og king of Bashan came out against us, he and all his people, for battle at Edrei.

verses.rationale: Preserves the no-fear command and explicit comparison of the two kings.
verses.before: The LORD said to me, ‘Do not fear him, for I have given him, all his people, and his land into your hand. You will do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon.’
verses.after: The LORD said to me, ‘Do not be afraid of him. I have handed him over to you, with all his people and his land. Do to him what you did to Sihon, the Amorite king who lived in Heshbon.’
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to me, ‘Do not fear him, for I have given him, all his people, and his land into your hand. You shall do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon.’

verses.rationale: Retains divine agency and the stated absence of survivors without softening the violence.
verses.before: So the LORD our God also gave into our hand Og king of Bashan and all his people, and we struck him until no survivor remained to him.
verses.after: So the LORD our God handed Og king of Bashan and all his people over to us too. We struck them down until no survivor remained.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the LORD our God also gave into our hand Og king of Bashan and all his people, and we struck him until no survivor remained to him.

verses.rationale: Keeps the exact sixty-town count and the emphatic completeness of capture.
verses.before: We captured all his cities at that time. There was not a town that we did not take from them: sixty cities, all the region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
verses.after: At that time we captured all his towns. There was not one we failed to take: sixty towns, the whole region of Argob, Og's kingdom in Bashan.
verses.tsw_comparator: We captured all his cities at that time. There was not a town that we did not take from them: sixty cities, all the region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.

verses.rationale: Preserves the fortification details and distinguishes the additional unwalled settlements.
verses.before: All these were cities fortified with high walls, gates, and bars, besides very many unwalled villages.
verses.after: All these towns were fortified with high walls, gates, and bars, besides a great many unwalled towns.
verses.tsw_comparator: All these were cities fortified with high walls, gates, and bars, besides very many unwalled villages.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated ban language and the named human victims, linking the account to Sihon's defeat.
verses.before: We devoted them to destruction, as we had done to Sihon king of Heshbon, devoting every city—men, women, and little children.
verses.after: We devoted them to destruction, as we had done to Sihon king of Heshbon, devoting every town to destruction—men, women, and little children.
verses.tsw_comparator: We devoted them to destruction, as we had done to Sihon king of Heshbon, devoting every city—men, women, and little children.

verses.rationale: Keeps the exception for livestock and goods separate from the destruction of inhabitants.
verses.before: But all the livestock and the spoil of the cities we took as plunder for ourselves.
verses.after: But we took all the livestock and the spoil of the towns as plunder for ourselves.
verses.tsw_comparator: But all the livestock and the spoil of the cities we took as plunder for ourselves.

verses.rationale: Preserves the two-king summary and southern and northern limits.
verses.before: “So at that time we took the land from the hand of the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, from the Wadi Arnon as far as Mount Hermon—
verses.after: At that time we took the land of the two Amorite kings beyond the Jordan, from the Wadi Arnon to Mount Hermon.
verses.tsw_comparator: “So at that time we took the land from the hand of the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, from the Wadi Arnon as far as Mount Hermon—

verses.rationale: Retains both peoples' names for Hermon without standardizing them away.
verses.before: the Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, and the Amorites call it Senir—
verses.after: The Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, while the Amorites call it Senir.
verses.tsw_comparator: the Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, and the Amorites call it Senir—

verses.rationale: Preserves the regional sequence, repeated all, and named endpoints.
verses.before: all the cities of the tableland, all Gilead, and all Bashan as far as Salecah and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
verses.after: We took all the towns of the plateau, all Gilead, and all Bashan as far as Salecah and Edrei, towns in Og's kingdom of Bashan.
verses.tsw_comparator: all the cities of the tableland, all Gilead, and all Bashan as far as Salecah and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan.

verses.rationale: Keeps the bed's material and dimensions without inferring Og's height; the note records the disputed object identification.
verses.before: For only Og king of Bashan remained from the remnant of the Rephaim. Look, his bed was a bed of iron. Is it not in Rabbah of the children of Ammon? Nine cubits was its length and four cubits its width, by the ordinary cubit.
verses.after: Only Og king of Bashan remained of the remnant of the Rephaim. His bed was made of iron—is it not in Rabbah of the Ammonites? It was nine cubits long and four cubits wide, measured by the ordinary human cubit.
verses.tsw_comparator: For only Og king of Bashan remained from the remnant of the Rephaim. Look, his bed was a bed of iron. Is it not in Rabbah of the children of Ammon? Nine cubits was its length and four cubits its width, by the ordinary cubit.

verses.rationale: Retains the allocation to both tribes and the limited half of Gilead.
verses.before: “This land we possessed at that time. From Aroer, which is on the edge of the Wadi Arnon, and half the hill country of Gilead with its cities, I gave to the Reubenites and the Gadites.
verses.after: When we took possession of this land, I gave the Reubenites and Gadites the territory from Aroer by the Wadi Arnon, along with half the hill country of Gilead and its towns.
verses.tsw_comparator: “This land we possessed at that time. From Aroer, which is on the edge of the Wadi Arnon, and half the hill country of Gilead with its cities, I gave to the Reubenites and the Gadites.

verses.rationale: Keeps the complementary allocation and the region's traditional designation.
verses.before: The rest of Gilead and all Bashan, the kingdom of Og, I gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh—all the region of Argob. All Bashan was called the land of Rephaim.
verses.after: I gave the rest of Gilead and all Bashan, Og's kingdom, to the half-tribe of Manasseh. The whole region of Argob, all that part of Bashan, is called the land of Rephaim.
verses.tsw_comparator: The rest of Gilead and all Bashan, the kingdom of Og, I gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh—all the region of Argob. All Bashan was called the land of Rephaim.

verses.rationale: Uses descendant for the lineage designation and preserves both boundary peoples and the commemorative settlement name.
verses.before: Jair son of Manasseh took all the region of Argob as far as the border of the Geshurites and Maacathites and called them, that is Bashan, after his own name, Havvoth-Jair, to this day.
verses.after: Jair, a descendant of Manasseh, took the whole region of Argob as far as the border of the Geshurites and Maacathites. He named Bashan's settlements after himself, Havvoth-jair, as they are called to this day.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jair son of Manasseh took all the region of Argob as far as the border of the Geshurites and Maacathites and called them, that is Bashan, after his own name, Havvoth-Jair, to this day.

verses.rationale: Retains the concise named grant without adding a territorial reconciliation.
verses.before: To Machir I gave Gilead.
verses.after: I gave Gilead to Machir.
verses.tsw_comparator: To Machir I gave Gilead.

verses.rationale: Keeps the middle-of-wadi boundary and the distinct northern boundary.
verses.before: To the Reubenites and the Gadites I gave from Gilead as far as the Wadi Arnon, the middle of the wadi as a border, and as far as the Wadi Jabbok, the border of the children of Ammon,
verses.after: To the Reubenites and Gadites I gave the territory from Gilead to the Wadi Arnon, with the middle of the wadi as its boundary, and as far as the Wadi Jabbok, the Ammonite boundary.
verses.tsw_comparator: To the Reubenites and the Gadites I gave from Gilead as far as the Wadi Arnon, the middle of the wadi as a border, and as far as the Wadi Jabbok, the border of the children of Ammon,

verses.rationale: Preserves the river boundary, both sea names, and the eastern slopes.
verses.before: and the Arabah, with the Jordan as a border, from Chinnereth as far as the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, under the slopes of Pisgah toward the sunrise.
verses.after: It also included the Arabah, with the Jordan as its boundary, from Chinnereth to the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, below the slopes of Pisgah on the east.
verses.tsw_comparator: and the Arabah, with the Jordan as a border, from Chinnereth as far as the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, under the slopes of Pisgah toward the sunrise.

verses.rationale: Keeps the eastern tribes' obligation to lead their brothers despite already receiving land.
verses.before: “I commanded you at that time, saying, ‘The LORD your God has given you this land to possess. All your warriors will cross over armed before your brothers, the children of Israel.
verses.after: At that time I commanded you, ‘The LORD your God has given you this land to possess. All your fighting men must cross over armed ahead of your brothers, the Israelites.
verses.tsw_comparator: “I commanded you at that time, saying, ‘The LORD your God has given you this land to possess. All your warriors shall cross over armed before your brothers, the children of Israel.

verses.rationale: Retains Moses' parenthetical observation and the three groups left behind.
verses.before: Only your wives, your little children, and your livestock—I know that you have much livestock—will remain in your cities that I have given you,
verses.after: Only your wives, little ones, and livestock—I know you have much livestock—may stay in the towns I have given you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Only your wives, your little children, and your livestock—I know that you have much livestock—shall remain in your cities that I have given you,

verses.rationale: Preserves rest as shared inheritance language and makes the condition for returning clear.
verses.before: until the LORD gives rest to your brothers as to you, and they also possess the land that the LORD your God is giving them beyond the Jordan. Then each of you may return to the possession that I have given you.’
verses.after: Stay until the LORD gives your brothers rest as he has given you, and they too possess the land the LORD your God is giving them beyond the Jordan. Then each of you may return to the possession I have given you.’
verses.tsw_comparator: until the LORD gives rest to your brothers as to you, and they also possess the land that the LORD your God is giving them beyond the Jordan. Then each of you may return to the possession that I have given you.’

verses.rationale: Retains eyewitness assurance and the two-kings comparison addressed to Joshua.
verses.before: “I commanded Joshua at that time, saying, ‘Your eyes have seen all that the LORD your God has done to these two kings. So the LORD will do to all the kingdoms into which you are crossing.
verses.after: At that time I commanded Joshua, ‘Your own eyes have seen everything the LORD your God did to these two kings. The LORD will do the same to all the kingdoms you are about to enter.’
verses.tsw_comparator: “I commanded Joshua at that time, saying, ‘Your eyes have seen all that the LORD your God has done to these two kings. So the LORD will do to all the kingdoms into which you are crossing.

verses.rationale: Preserves the plural encouragement to the people and God's fighting role.
verses.before: You will not fear them, for the LORD your God is the one fighting for you.’
verses.after: Do not be afraid of them, for the LORD your God is the one who fights for you.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not fear them, for the LORD your God is the one fighting for you.’

verses.rationale: Keeps pleading rather than neutral asking and lets the prayer follow across the label.
verses.before: “I pleaded with the LORD at that time, saying,
verses.after: At that time I pleaded with the LORD,
verses.tsw_comparator: “I pleaded with the LORD at that time, saying,

verses.rationale: Distinguishes Adonai YHWH as Lord GOD and retains the rhetorical comparison and strong-hand image.
verses.before: ‘Lord GOD, you have begun to show your servant your greatness and your strong hand, for what god is there in the heavens or on the earth who can do according to your works and according to your mighty acts?
verses.after: ‘Lord GOD, you have begun to show your servant your greatness and your strong hand. What god in heaven or on earth can do deeds and mighty acts like yours?
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘Lord GOD, you have begun to show your servant your greatness and your strong hand, for what god is there in the heavens or on the earth who can do according to your works and according to your mighty acts?

verses.rationale: Keeps the plea to cross and see, with repeated good and the northern region.
verses.before: Please let me cross over and see the good land beyond the Jordan, this good hill country and Lebanon.’
verses.after: Please let me cross over and see the good land beyond the Jordan, that good hill country and Lebanon.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Please let me cross over and see the good land beyond the Jordan, this good hill country and Lebanon.’

verses.rationale: Preserves Moses' causal accusation and the force of the refusal in direct speech.
verses.before: But the LORD was furious with me because of you and would not listen to me. The LORD said to me, ‘Enough for you! Do not speak to me again about this matter.
verses.after: But the LORD was furious with me because of you and would not listen to me. He said, ‘Enough! Do not speak to me about this again.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the LORD was furious with me because of you and would not listen to me. The LORD said to me, ‘Enough for you! Do not speak to me again about this matter.

verses.rationale: Retains all four directions in source order and the contrast between seeing and crossing.
verses.before: Go up to the top of Pisgah and lift your eyes westward, northward, southward, and eastward, and see with your eyes, for you will not cross this Jordan.
verses.after: Go up to the top of Pisgah. Look west, north, south, and east, and see it with your own eyes, because you will not cross this Jordan.
verses.tsw_comparator: Go up to the top of Pisgah and lift your eyes westward, northward, southward, and eastward, and see with your eyes, for you shall not cross this Jordan.

verses.rationale: Keeps the three commissioning actions and Joshua's role contrasted with Moses' limited sight.
verses.before: But command Joshua, strengthen him and make him courageous, for he will cross over before this people and he will cause them to inherit the land that you will see.’
verses.after: Commission Joshua. Strengthen him and give him courage, because he will cross over ahead of this people and lead them into possession of the land you will see.’
verses.tsw_comparator: But command Joshua, strengthen him and make him courageous, for he shall cross over before this people and he shall cause them to inherit the land that you will see.’

verses.rationale: Retains the closing location as the setting for the address that follows.
verses.before: So we remained in the valley opposite Beth-Peor.
verses.after: So we stayed in the valley opposite Beth-peor.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So we remained in the valley opposite Beth-Peor.

verses.rationale: Keeps hearing directed toward doing and the sequence life, entry, and possession.
verses.before: “And now, Israel, listen to the statutes and the judgments that I am teaching you to do, so that you may live and go in and possess the land that the LORD, the God of your ancestors, is giving you.
verses.after: “Now, Israel, listen to the statutes and rulings I am teaching you to practice. Then you may live, enter the land, and take possession of what the LORD, the God of your fathers, is giving you.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And now, Israel, listen to the statutes and the judgments that I am teaching you to do, so that you may live and go in and possess the land that the LORD, the God of your ancestors, is giving you.

verses.rationale: Preserves both boundaries on alteration and the positive command to keep the instruction.
verses.before: You will not add to the word that I command you, and you will not take away from it, so that you may keep the commandments of the LORD your God that I command you.
verses.after: Do not add to what I command you or take anything away from it. Keep the commands of the LORD your God that I am giving you.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not add to the word that I command you, and you shall not take away from it, so that you may keep the commandments of the LORD your God that I command you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the named event and its interpretation as destruction for following Baal.
verses.before: Your eyes have seen what the LORD did at Baal-Peor, for every man who went after the Baal of Peor, the LORD your God destroyed from your midst.
verses.after: Your own eyes saw what the LORD did at Baal-peor. The LORD your God destroyed from among you everyone who followed Baal of Peor.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your eyes have seen what the LORD did at Baal-Peor, for every man who went after the Baal of Peor, the LORD your God destroyed from your midst.

verses.rationale: Retains the physical cling image and the contrast with the dead followers of Baal.
verses.before: But you who clung to the LORD your God are all alive today.
verses.after: But all of you who cling to the LORD your God are alive today.
verses.tsw_comparator: But you who clung to the LORD your God are all alive today.

verses.rationale: Preserves Moses' commissioned teaching and its intended setting and practice.
verses.before: “See, I have taught you statutes and judgments, as the LORD my God commanded me, so that you may do so among the land that you are entering to possess.
verses.after: See, I have taught you statutes and rulings as the LORD my God commanded me, so that you may practice them in the land you are entering to possess.
verses.tsw_comparator: “See, I have taught you statutes and judgments, as the LORD my God commanded me, so that you may do so in the midst of the land that you are entering to possess.

verses.rationale: Keeps public recognition tied to practiced instruction and repeats wisdom and understanding in the response.
verses.before: Keep them and do them, for this will be your wisdom and your understanding in the eyes of the peoples, who will hear all these statutes and say, ‘Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.’
verses.after: Keep them and put them into practice. This will be your wisdom and understanding in the eyes of the peoples, who will hear all these statutes and say, ‘Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people!’
verses.tsw_comparator: Keep them and do them, for this will be your wisdom and your understanding in the eyes of the peoples, who will hear all these statutes and say, ‘Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.’

verses.rationale: Renders the comparative elohim phrase with a singular god while noting the possible plural gods reading.
verses.before: For what great nation is there that has a god so near to it as the LORD our God is whenever we call to him?
verses.after: For what great nation has a god so near to it as the LORD our God is to us whenever we call on him?
verses.tsw_comparator: For what great nation is there that has a god so near to it as the LORD our God is whenever we call to him?

verses.rationale: Retains the parallel great-nation question and righteous as a property of the instruction.
verses.before: And what great nation is there that has statutes and judgments as righteous as all this instruction that I am setting before you today?
verses.after: And what great nation has statutes and rulings as righteous as this whole instruction I am setting before you today?
verses.tsw_comparator: And what great nation is there that has statutes and judgments as righteous as all this instruction that I am setting before you today?

verses.rationale: Preserves the eyes-heart-memory sequence and the duty to pass it through generations.
verses.before: “Only guard yourself and guard your life diligently, lest you forget the things that your eyes have seen and lest they depart from your heart all the days of your life. Make them known to your children and your children’s children—
verses.after: Only be careful. Watch yourself closely, so that you do not forget what your eyes have seen or let it leave your heart all the days of your life. Make it known to your children and grandchildren.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Only guard yourself and guard your life diligently, lest you forget the things that your eyes have seen and lest they depart from your heart all the days of your life. Make them known to your children and your children’s children—

verses.rationale: Makes the recalled day readable while retaining hearing, lifelong fear, and children's instruction.
verses.before: the day you stood before the LORD your God at Horeb, when the LORD said to me, ‘Gather the people to me, and I will make them hear my words, so that they may learn to fear me all the days that they live on the ground and may teach their children.’
verses.after: Remember the day you stood before the LORD your God at Horeb, when the LORD told me, ‘Gather the people to me so I can let them hear my words. Then they may learn to fear me all the days they live on earth and teach their children.’
verses.tsw_comparator: the day you stood before the LORD your God at Horeb, when the LORD said to me, ‘Gather the people to me, and I will make them hear my words, so that they may learn to fear me all the days that they live on the ground and may teach their children.’

verses.rationale: Keeps the towering fire image and threefold obscurity rather than flattening the scene.
verses.before: You came near and stood at the foot of the mountain, and the mountain burned with fire to the heart of the heavens, with darkness, cloud, and thick darkness.
verses.after: You came near and stood at the foot of the mountain. The mountain blazed with fire to the heart of the heavens, amid darkness, cloud, and thick gloom.
verses.tsw_comparator: You came near and stood at the foot of the mountain, and the mountain burned with fire to the heart of the heavens, with darkness, cloud, and thick darkness.

verses.rationale: Preserves the pivotal distinction between audible speech and unseen form.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to you from the midst of the fire. You heard the sound of words, but you saw no form—only a voice.
verses.after: The LORD spoke to you from the fire. You heard the sound of words, but saw no form—only a voice.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to you from the midst of the fire. You heard the sound of words, but you saw no form—only a voice.

verses.rationale: Retains the source's Ten Words designation, covenant obligation, and two tablets, with vocabulary for recognition.
verses.before: He declared to you his covenant that he commanded you to do, the Ten Words, and he wrote them on two tablets of stone.
verses.after: He declared his covenant to you, commanding you to keep the Ten Words, and he wrote them on two stone tablets.
verses.tsw_comparator: He declared to you his covenant that he commanded you to do, the Ten Words, and he wrote them on two tablets of stone.

verses.rationale: Keeps teaching and practice linked to the imminent crossing.
verses.before: And the LORD commanded me at that time to teach you statutes and judgments, so that you might do them in the land that you are crossing over to possess.
verses.after: At that time the LORD commanded me to teach you statutes and rulings, so that you would practice them in the land you are crossing over to possess.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD commanded me at that time to teach you statutes and judgments, so that you might do them in the land that you are crossing over to possess.

verses.rationale: Repeats the absence of visible form as the stated basis for the warning.
verses.before: “So guard your lives diligently, for you saw no form on the day the LORD spoke to you at Horeb from the midst of the fire,
verses.after: So watch yourselves closely. You saw no form on the day the LORD spoke to you at Horeb from the fire.
verses.tsw_comparator: “So guard your lives diligently, for you saw no form on the day the LORD spoke to you at Horeb from the midst of the fire,

verses.rationale: Preserves the corruption warning and both human sexes as the beginning of the image list.
verses.before: lest you act corruptly and make for yourselves a carved image in the form of any figure, the likeness of male or female,
verses.after: Do not corrupt yourselves by making a carved image in the shape of any figure, whether male or female,
verses.tsw_comparator: lest you act corruptly and make for yourselves a carved image in the form of any figure, the likeness of male or female,

verses.rationale: Retains the terrestrial and aerial categories without closing the continuing list.
verses.before: the likeness of any animal that is on the earth, the likeness of any winged bird that flies in the heavens,
verses.after: or in the shape of any animal on earth, any winged bird flying in the sky,
verses.tsw_comparator: the likeness of any animal that is on the earth, the likeness of any winged bird that flies in the heavens,

verses.rationale: Preserves creeping creatures and the ancient spatial description of the waters.
verses.before: the likeness of anything that creeps on the ground, the likeness of any fish that is in the water beneath the earth.
verses.after: anything that creeps along the ground, or any fish in the waters below the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: the likeness of anything that creeps on the ground, the likeness of any fish that is in the water beneath the earth.

verses.rationale: Keeps the heavenly host and allotment claim without adding a permission for other peoples' worship.
verses.before: And lest you lift your eyes to the heavens and see the sun, moon, and stars, all the host of the heavens, and be drawn away and bow down to them and serve them—things that the LORD your God allotted to all the peoples under the whole heavens.
verses.after: When you look up to the heavens and see the sun, moon, and stars, all the host of heaven, do not be drawn away to bow down to them and serve them. The LORD your God has allotted them to all the peoples everywhere under heaven.
verses.tsw_comparator: And lest you lift your eyes to the heavens and see the sun, moon, and stars, all the host of the heavens, and be drawn away and bow down to them and serve them—things that the LORD your God allotted to all the peoples under the whole heavens.

verses.rationale: Retains Egypt's iron-furnace image and Israel as God's inheritance.
verses.before: But the LORD took you and brought you out from the iron furnace, from Egypt, to be for him a people of inheritance, as you are this day.
verses.after: But the LORD took you and brought you out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt, to be the people of his own inheritance, as you are today.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the LORD took you and brought you out from the iron furnace, from Egypt, to be for him a people of inheritance, as you are this day.

verses.rationale: Keeps Moses' recurring account of his exclusion and the oath's two prohibitions.
verses.before: “The LORD was angry with me because of your words and swore that I would not cross the Jordan and would not enter the good land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.
verses.after: The LORD was angry with me because of you. He swore that I would not cross the Jordan or enter the good land the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.
verses.tsw_comparator: “The LORD was angry with me because of your words and swore that I would not cross the Jordan and would not enter the good land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.

verses.rationale: Preserves the emphatic contrast between Moses' death and the people's entry.
verses.before: For I will die in this land; I will not cross the Jordan. But you are crossing over and will possess this good land.
verses.after: I will die in this land. I will not cross the Jordan, but you will cross and take possession of that good land.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I will die in this land; I will not cross the Jordan. But you are crossing over and will possess this good land.

verses.rationale: Connects forgotten covenant with prohibited images while unfolding the compressed command phrase.
verses.before: Guard yourselves, lest you forget the covenant of the LORD your God that he made with you and make for yourselves a carved image, the form of anything that the LORD your God has forbidden you.
verses.after: Watch yourselves, so that you do not forget the covenant the LORD your God made with you and make yourselves a carved image in any form the LORD your God has forbidden.
verses.tsw_comparator: Guard yourselves, lest you forget the covenant of the LORD your God that he made with you and make for yourselves a carved image, the form of anything that the LORD your God has forbidden you.

verses.rationale: Retains both forceful divine descriptions without substituting a milder emotional term.
verses.before: For the LORD your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God.
verses.after: For the LORD your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the LORD your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God.

verses.rationale: Keeps the generational setting and conditional warning open into its consequence.
verses.before: “When you father children and children’s children and have grown old in the land, if you act corruptly and make a carved image in the form of anything and do what is evil in the eyes of the LORD your God to provoke him to anger,
verses.after: When you have children and grandchildren and have lived long in the land, if you corrupt yourselves by making a carved image of any kind and do what is evil in the eyes of the LORD your God, provoking him to anger,
verses.tsw_comparator: “When you father children and children’s children and have grown old in the land, if you act corruptly and make a carved image in the form of anything and do what is evil in the eyes of the LORD your God to provoke him to anger,

verses.rationale: Preserves the cosmic witnesses and repeated threat without weakening the destruction language.
verses.before: I call the heavens and the earth to witness against you today that you will surely perish quickly from the land that you are crossing the Jordan to possess. You will not prolong your days upon it but will surely be destroyed.
verses.after: I call heaven and earth as witnesses against you today: you will quickly perish from the land you are crossing the Jordan to possess. You will not live long in it. You will be utterly destroyed.
verses.tsw_comparator: I call the heavens and the earth to witness against you today that you will surely perish quickly from the land that you are crossing the Jordan to possess. You will not prolong your days upon it but will surely be destroyed.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine scattering and the contrast between dispersed peoples and few survivors.
verses.before: The LORD will scatter you among the peoples, and you will be left few in number among the nations where the LORD drives you.
verses.after: The LORD will scatter you among the peoples. Only a few of you will remain among the nations where the LORD drives you.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD will scatter you among the peoples, and you will be left few in number among the nations where the LORD drives you.

verses.rationale: Retains the material contrast and all four absent senses or actions.
verses.before: There you will serve gods, the work of human hands—wood and stone—which do not see or hear or eat or smell.
verses.after: There you will serve gods made by human hands, wood and stone, which cannot see, hear, eat, or smell.
