verses.tsw_comparator: There you will serve gods, the work of human hands—wood and stone—which do not see or hear or eat or smell.

verses.rationale: Preserves the from-there reversal and the conditional wholehearted search with heart and soul language.
verses.before: But from there you will seek the LORD your God, and you will find him if you search for him with all your heart and with all your life.
verses.after: But from there you will seek the LORD your God and find him, if you search for him with all your heart and all your soul.
verses.tsw_comparator: But from there you will seek the LORD your God, and you will find him if you search for him with all your heart and with all your life.

verses.rationale: Renders latter days as the coming horizon without specifying an end-time scheme; retains return and hearing.
verses.before: When you are in distress and all these things find you in the latter days, you will return to the LORD your God and listen to his voice.
verses.after: When you are in distress and all these things come upon you in the days ahead, you will return to the LORD your God and listen to his voice.
verses.tsw_comparator: When you are in distress and all these things find you in the latter days, you will return to the LORD your God and listen to his voice.

verses.rationale: Retains all three assurances alongside the preceding threats without resolving their tension editorially.
verses.before: For the LORD your God is a compassionate God. He will not abandon you or destroy you or forget the covenant with your ancestors that he swore to them.
verses.after: For the LORD your God is a merciful God. He will not abandon you or destroy you or forget the covenant he swore to your fathers.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the LORD your God is a compassionate God. He will not abandon you or destroy you or forget the covenant with your ancestors that he swore to them.

verses.rationale: Preserves the historical and cosmic scope of the inquiry and its paired rhetorical questions.
verses.before: “Indeed, ask now concerning the former days that were before you, from the day God created humanity upon the earth, and from one end of the heavens to the other: Has there ever been anything like this great thing, or has anything like it been heard?
verses.after: Ask about the days before you, from the day God created humanity on the earth. Ask from one end of the heavens to the other: Has anything this great ever happened, or has anything like it ever been heard?
verses.tsw_comparator: “Indeed, ask now concerning the former days that were before you, from the day God created humanity upon the earth, and from one end of the heavens to the other: Has there ever been anything like this great thing, or has anything like it been heard?

verses.rationale: Keeps the comparative question and the survival emphasis central to Horeb's recollection.
verses.before: Has a people ever heard the voice of God speaking from the midst of the fire, as you heard, and lived?
verses.after: Has any people heard the voice of a god speaking from the fire, as you have heard, and lived?
verses.tsw_comparator: Has a people ever heard the voice of God speaking from the midst of the fire, as you heard, and lived?

verses.rationale: Retains nation from nation and every item in the extended list of divine acts.
verses.before: Or has a god ever tried to go and take for himself a nation from the midst of another nation, by trials, signs, wonders, war, a strong hand, an outstretched arm, and great terrors, according to all that the LORD your God did for you in Egypt before your eyes?
verses.after: Or has a god ever attempted to take a nation for himself from within another nation, through trials, signs, wonders, war, a strong hand, an outstretched arm, and great terrors, as the LORD your God did for you in Egypt before your eyes?
verses.tsw_comparator: Or has a god ever tried to go and take for himself a nation from the midst of another nation, by trials, signs, wonders, war, a strong hand, an outstretched arm, and great terrors, according to all that the LORD your God did for you in Egypt before your eyes?

verses.rationale: Keeps the purpose of the demonstration and its exclusive conclusion.
verses.before: You were shown this so that you might know that the LORD—he is God; there is no other besides him.
verses.after: You were shown these things so that you would know that the LORD is God. There is no other besides him.
verses.tsw_comparator: You were shown this so that you might know that the LORD—he is God; there is no other besides him.

verses.rationale: Preserves the heaven-earth parallel and the movement from voice and sight to words.
verses.before: From the heavens he made you hear his voice to discipline you, and upon the earth he showed you his great fire, and you heard his words from the midst of the fire.
verses.after: From heaven he let you hear his voice to instruct you. On earth he let you see his great fire, and you heard his words from the fire.
verses.tsw_comparator: From the heavens he made you hear his voice to discipline you, and upon the earth he showed you his great fire, and you heard his words from the midst of the fire.

verses.rationale: Takes the singular ancestral suffix collectively with fathers; retains presence rather than inserting an angel and notes the grammatical shift.
verses.before: Because he loved your ancestors and chose their offspring after them, he brought you out from Egypt by his presence, by his great power,
verses.after: Because he loved your fathers and chose their descendants after them, he brought you out of Egypt by his presence and his great power,
verses.tsw_comparator: Because he loved your ancestors and chose their offspring after them, he brought you out from Egypt by his presence, by his great power,

verses.rationale: Keeps the three purposes of the exodus and the comparative strength of the displaced nations.
verses.before: to drive out before you nations greater and mightier than you, to bring you in and give you their land as an inheritance, as it is this day.
verses.after: to drive out before you nations greater and stronger than you, bring you in, and give you their land as an inheritance, as he has now done.
verses.tsw_comparator: to drive out before you nations greater and mightier than you, to bring you in and give you their land as an inheritance, as it is this day.

verses.rationale: Retains knowing and heart response, the vertical totality, and the repeated exclusive conclusion.
verses.before: Know therefore today and bring it back to your heart that the LORD—he is God in the heavens above and on the earth beneath; there is no other.
verses.after: Know this today and take it to heart: the LORD is God in heaven above and on earth below. There is no other.
verses.tsw_comparator: Know therefore today and bring it back to your heart that the LORD—he is God in the heavens above and on the earth beneath; there is no other.

verses.rationale: Preserves both welfare and length of days, the children's future, and the enduring gift.
verses.before: Keep his statutes and his commandments that I command you today, so that it may go well with you and with your children after you, and so that you may prolong your days upon the ground that the LORD your God is giving you for all days.
verses.after: Keep his statutes and commands that I am giving you today, so that it may go well with you and your children after you, and so that you may live long on the land the LORD your God is giving you for all time.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Keep his statutes and his commandments that I command you today, so that it may go well with you and with your children after you, and so that you may prolong your days upon the ground that the LORD your God is giving you for all days.

verses.rationale: Marks the narrator's return and retains the eastward orientation and town count.
verses.before: Then Moses set apart three cities beyond the Jordan toward the sunrise,
verses.after: Then Moses set apart three towns beyond the Jordan, toward the sunrise,
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Moses set apart three cities beyond the Jordan toward the sunrise,

verses.rationale: Distinguishes unintentional killing and absence of prior hatred without treating refuge as automatic acquittal.
verses.before: so that the manslayer who kills his neighbor unintentionally, without hating him previously, may flee there. He may flee to one of these cities and live:
verses.after: where someone could flee after killing a neighbor unintentionally, without having hated that neighbor beforehand. By fleeing to one of these towns, the killer could stay alive.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that the manslayer who kills his neighbor unintentionally, without hating him previously, may flee there. He may flee to one of these cities and live:

verses.rationale: Preserves all three town-region-tribe assignments.
verses.before: Bezer in the wilderness on the tableland for the Reubenites, Ramoth in Gilead for the Gadites, and Golan in Bashan for the Manassites.
verses.after: The towns were Bezer in the wilderness on the plateau for the Reubenites, Ramoth in Gilead for the Gadites, and Golan in Bashan for the Manassites.
verses.tsw_comparator: Bezer in the wilderness on the tableland for the Reubenites, Ramoth in Gilead for the Gadites, and Golan in Bashan for the Manassites.

verses.rationale: Keeps the new framing statement and instruction terminology.
verses.before: This is the instruction that Moses set before the children of Israel.
verses.after: This is the instruction Moses set before the Israelites.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is the instruction that Moses set before the children of Israel.

verses.rationale: Retains the three instruction categories and the departure setting, continuing into the location.
verses.before: These are the testimonies, statutes, and judgments that Moses spoke to the children of Israel when they came out from Egypt,
verses.after: These are the testimonies, statutes, and rulings Moses gave the Israelites when they came out of Egypt,
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the testimonies, statutes, and judgments that Moses spoke to the children of Israel when they came out from Egypt,

verses.rationale: Preserves the layered location and the repeated historical description of Sihon's defeat.
verses.before: beyond the Jordan, in the valley opposite Beth-Peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites who lived in Heshbon, whom Moses and the children of Israel struck when they came out from Egypt.
verses.after: beyond the Jordan, in the valley opposite Beth-peor, in the land of Sihon, the Amorite king who lived in Heshbon. Moses and the Israelites defeated him when they came out of Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: beyond the Jordan, in the valley opposite Beth-Peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites who lived in Heshbon, whom Moses and the children of Israel struck when they came out from Egypt.

verses.rationale: Keeps the two kings and the explicit eastern orientation.
verses.before: They possessed his land and the land of Og king of Bashan, the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan toward the sunrise,
verses.after: They took possession of his land and the land of Og king of Bashan, the two Amorite kings beyond the Jordan toward the sunrise.
verses.tsw_comparator: They possessed his land and the land of Og king of Bashan, the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan toward the sunrise,

verses.rationale: Preserves Sion as written here rather than silently changing it to Sirion or confusing it with Zion.
verses.before: from Aroer, which is on the edge of the Wadi Arnon, as far as Mount Sion—that is, Hermon—
verses.after: Their territory stretched from Aroer on the edge of the Wadi Arnon to Mount Sion, that is, Hermon,
verses.tsw_comparator: from Aroer, which is on the edge of the Wadi Arnon, as far as Mount Sion—that is, Hermon—

verses.rationale: Completes the territorial list with the eastern Arabah, sea, and slopes.
verses.before: and all the Arabah beyond the Jordan toward the sunrise, as far as the Sea of the Arabah, under the slopes of Pisgah.
verses.after: and included all the Arabah east of the Jordan, as far as the Sea of the Arabah below the slopes of Pisgah.
verses.tsw_comparator: and all the Arabah beyond the Jordan toward the sunrise, as far as the Sea of the Arabah, under the slopes of Pisgah.

verses.rationale: Preserves the collective summons, repeated hearing, and movement from learning to doing.
verses.before: Moses called all Israel and said to them, “Hear, Israel, the statutes and judgments that I speak in your hearing today. Learn them and be careful to do them.
verses.after: Moses summoned all Israel and said to them, “Hear, Israel, the statutes and rulings I am speaking in your hearing today. Learn them and be careful to put them into practice.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses called all Israel and said to them, “Hear, Israel, the statutes and judgments that I speak in your hearing today. Learn them and be careful to do them.

verses.rationale: Keeps the first-person communal claim and the named covenant location.
verses.before: The LORD our God made a covenant with us at Horeb.
verses.after: The LORD our God made a covenant with us at Horeb.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD our God made a covenant with us at Horeb.

verses.rationale: Retains the source's emphatic not-but contrast without adding not only to harmonize generations.
verses.before: Not with our ancestors alone did the LORD make this covenant, but with us, all of us who are alive here today.
verses.after: The LORD did not make this covenant with our fathers, but with us—all of us who are here alive today.
verses.tsw_comparator: Not with our ancestors alone did the LORD make this covenant, but with us, all of us who are alive here today.

verses.rationale: Preserves face-to-face language alongside the earlier insistence that no form was seen.
verses.before: Face to face the LORD spoke with you on the mountain from the midst of the fire—
verses.after: The LORD spoke with you face to face on the mountain, from the fire.
verses.tsw_comparator: Face to face the LORD spoke with you on the mountain from the midst of the fire—

verses.rationale: Keeps Moses' mediation and the people's fear while introducing the LORD's quoted words.
verses.before: I was standing between the LORD and you at that time to declare to you the word of the LORD, for you were afraid because of the fire and did not go up the mountain—saying:
verses.after: At that time I stood between the LORD and you to declare the LORD's word to you, because you were afraid of the fire and did not go up the mountain. He said,
verses.tsw_comparator: I was standing between the LORD and you at that time to declare to you the word of the LORD, for you were afraid because of the fire and did not go up the mountain—saying:

verses.rationale: Keeps the divine self-identification and liberation from a house of slavery as the commands' foundation.
verses.before: “I am the LORD your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt, from the house of slavery.
verses.after: ‘I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
verses.tsw_comparator: “I am the LORD your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt, from the house of slavery.

verses.rationale: Retains before me and explains its exclusivity in a note rather than reducing it to a ranking of gods.
verses.before: You will have no other gods before me.
verses.after: You must have no other gods before me.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall have no other gods before me.

verses.rationale: Keeps the three spatial realms and the distinction between carved image and likeness.
verses.before: You will not make for yourself a carved image, any form of what is in the heavens above, on the earth beneath, or in the waters under the earth.
verses.after: You must not make yourself a carved image or any likeness of what is in heaven above, on earth below, or in the waters below the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not make for yourself a carved image, any form of what is in the heavens above, on the earth beneath, or in the waters under the earth.

verses.rationale: Preserves the difficult intergenerational consequence and jealous designation without removing either agency or scope.
verses.before: You will not bow down to them or serve them, for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, attending to the guilt of fathers upon children to the third and fourth generation of people who hate me,
verses.after: You must not bow down to them or serve them. For I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, calling children to account for their fathers' guilt to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me,
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not bow down to them or serve them, for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, attending to the guilt of fathers upon children to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me,

verses.rationale: Follows the read form my commands against written his commands and retains thousands without silently adding generations.
verses.before: but showing steadfast love to thousands of people who love me and keep my commandments.
verses.after: but showing faithful love to thousands of those who love me and keep my commands.
verses.tsw_comparator: but showing steadfast love to thousands of those who love me and keep my commandments.

verses.rationale: Renders the name-bearing prohibition with falsehood while noting the wider emptiness or worthlessness range.
verses.before: You will not carry the name of the LORD your God for emptiness, for the LORD will not hold innocent anyone who carries his name for emptiness.
verses.after: You must not use the name of the LORD your God for falsehood, because the LORD will not hold anyone guiltless who uses his name for falsehood.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not carry the name of the LORD your God for emptiness, for the LORD will not hold innocent anyone who carries his name for emptiness.

verses.rationale: Retains observe rather than harmonizing Exodus' remember and preserves the prior-command reference.
verses.before: Keep the Sabbath day to consecrate it, as the LORD your God commanded you.
verses.after: Observe the Sabbath day and keep it holy, as the LORD your God commanded you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Keep the Sabbath day to consecrate it, as the LORD your God commanded you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the six-day work span and lets its contrast continue into the seventh day.
verses.before: Six days you will labor and do all your work,
verses.after: For six days you are to labor and do all your work,
verses.tsw_comparator: Six days you shall labor and do all your work,

verses.rationale: Preserves every named dependent and animal and the explicit equal-rest purpose for enslaved people.
verses.before: but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God. You will not do any work—you, your son, your daughter, your male servant, your female servant, your ox, your donkey, any of your livestock, or the resident alien who is within your gates—so that your male servant and female servant may rest as you do.
verses.after: but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God. You must not do any work—you, your son or daughter, your male or female slave, your ox or donkey or any of your livestock, or the resident foreigner within your gates—so that your male and female slaves may rest as you do.
verses.tsw_comparator: but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God. You shall not do any work—you, your son, your daughter, your male servant, your female servant, your ox, your donkey, any of your livestock, or the resident alien who is within your gates—so that your male servant and female servant may rest as you do.

verses.rationale: Keeps enslavement and liberation as this account's Sabbath rationale rather than importing the creation rationale from Exodus.
verses.before: You will remember that you were a servant in the land of Egypt, and the LORD your God brought you out from there with a strong hand and an outstretched arm. Therefore the LORD your God commanded you to keep the Sabbath day.
verses.after: Remember that you were a slave in Egypt and that the LORD your God brought you out with a strong hand and an outstretched arm. That is why the LORD your God commanded you to observe the Sabbath day.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall remember that you were a servant in the land of Egypt, and the LORD your God brought you out from there with a strong hand and an outstretched arm. Therefore the LORD your God commanded you to keep the Sabbath day.

verses.rationale: Preserves both parents, the command reference, and the paired promises of longevity and welfare.
verses.before: Honor your father and your mother, as the LORD your God commanded you, so that your days may be long and so that it may go well with you upon the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
verses.after: Honor your father and your mother, as the LORD your God commanded you, so that you may live long and it may go well with you in the land the LORD your God is giving you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Honor your father and your mother, as the LORD your God commanded you, so that your days may be long and so that it may go well with you upon the land that the LORD your God is giving you.

verses.rationale: Uses murder for the prohibited culpable taking of human life, maintaining the distinction from every occurrence of killing.
verses.before: You will not murder.
verses.after: You must not murder.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not murder.

verses.rationale: Retains the recognizable covenant prohibition without replacing the specific act with generic unfaithfulness.
verses.before: You will not commit adultery.
verses.after: You must not commit adultery.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not commit adultery.

verses.rationale: Keeps the brief unqualified prohibition without narrowing its object beyond the source.
verses.before: You will not steal.
verses.after: You must not steal.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not steal.

verses.rationale: Makes the witnessing action natural in English while preserving its target and falsity.
verses.before: You will not answer against your neighbor as a false witness.
verses.after: You must not testify falsely against your neighbor.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not answer against your neighbor as a false witness.

verses.rationale: Preserves the wife-first order, distinct desire verbs, field, enslaved people, and full possession list without harmonizing Exodus.
verses.before: You will not desire your neighbor’s wife. You will not crave your neighbor’s house, his field, his male servant, his female servant, his ox, his donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.
verses.after: You must not covet your neighbor's wife. You must not desire your neighbor's house or field, male or female slave, ox or donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.’
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not desire your neighbor’s wife. You shall not crave your neighbor’s house, his field, his male servant, his female servant, his ox, his donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.

verses.rationale: Retains the complete assembly, sensory setting, completion of the direct address, and two stone tablets.
verses.before: “These words the LORD spoke to all your assembly on the mountain from the midst of the fire, cloud, and thick darkness, with a great voice, and he added no more. He wrote them on two tablets of stone and gave them to me.
verses.after: The LORD spoke these words to your whole assembly on the mountain, from the fire, cloud, and thick gloom, with a mighty voice. He added no more. He wrote them on two stone tablets and gave them to me.
verses.tsw_comparator: “These words the LORD spoke to all your assembly on the mountain from the midst of the fire, cloud, and thick darkness, with a great voice, and he added no more. He wrote them on two tablets of stone and gave them to me.

verses.rationale: Preserves the voice-darkness-fire setting and both groups of representatives.
verses.before: When you heard the voice from the midst of the darkness while the mountain burned with fire, you came near to me, all the heads of your tribes and your elders.
verses.after: When you heard the voice from the darkness while the mountain blazed with fire, all your tribal leaders and elders came to me.
verses.tsw_comparator: When you heard the voice from the midst of the darkness while the mountain burned with fire, you came near to me, all the heads of your tribes and your elders.

verses.rationale: Keeps the people's acknowledgment of revelation and surviving divine speech.
verses.before: You said, ‘Look, the LORD our God has shown us his glory and greatness, and we have heard his voice from the midst of the fire. This day we have seen that God speaks with humanity and a person lives.
verses.after: You said, ‘The LORD our God has shown us his glory and greatness, and we have heard his voice from the fire. Today we have seen that God can speak with a human being and that person can live.
verses.tsw_comparator: You said, ‘Look, the LORD our God has shown us his glory and greatness, and we have heard his voice from the midst of the fire. This day we have seen that God speaks with humanity and a person lives.

verses.rationale: Preserves the fearful question and repeated death claim rather than resolving the tension with their survival.
verses.before: And now why should we die? For this great fire will consume us. If we continue to hear the voice of the LORD our God any longer, we will die.
verses.after: But now, why should we die? This great fire will consume us. If we keep hearing the voice of the LORD our God, we will die.
verses.tsw_comparator: And now why should we die? For this great fire will consume us. If we continue to hear the voice of the LORD our God any longer, we will die.

verses.rationale: Keeps all flesh and living God in the rhetorical comparison.
verses.before: For who is there of all flesh who has heard the voice of the living God speaking from the midst of the fire as we have and lived?
verses.after: For who of all flesh has heard the voice of the living God speaking from the fire, as we have, and lived?
verses.tsw_comparator: For who is there of all flesh who has heard the voice of the living God speaking from the midst of the fire as we have and lived?

verses.rationale: Preserves the proposed mediation and the people's commitment to both hearing and doing.
verses.before: You go near and hear all that the LORD our God says. Then you speak to us all that the LORD our God speaks to you, and we will hear and do it.’
verses.after: You go near and hear everything the LORD our God says. Then tell us everything the LORD our God tells you, and we will listen and do it.’
verses.tsw_comparator: You go near and hear all that the LORD our God says. Then you speak to us all that the LORD our God speaks to you, and we will hear and do it.’

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated hearing and divine approval of the mediation request.
verses.before: “The LORD heard the sound of your words when you spoke to me, and the LORD said to me, ‘I have heard the sound of the words of this people that they spoke to you. All that they have spoken is good.
verses.after: The LORD heard what you said when you spoke to me. He told me, ‘I have heard what this people said to you. Everything they have said is right.
verses.tsw_comparator: “The LORD heard the sound of your words when you spoke to me, and the LORD said to me, ‘I have heard the sound of the words of this people that they spoke to you. All that they have spoken is good.

verses.rationale: Preserves the divine wish rather than turning it into a prediction and keeps heart, fear, and enduring obedience together.
verses.before: If only they had such a heart in them to fear me and keep all my commandments all the days, so that it might go well with them and with their children forever!
verses.after: If only they had such a heart as this—to fear me and keep all my commands always—so that it might go well with them and their children forever!
verses.tsw_comparator: If only they had such a heart in them to fear me and keep all my commandments all the days, so that it might go well with them and with their children forever!

verses.rationale: Renders the nested direct instruction smoothly without changing its addressees or destination.
verses.before: Go, say to them, “Return to your tents.”
verses.after: Go and tell them to return to their tents.
verses.tsw_comparator: Go, say to them, “Return to your tents.”

verses.rationale: Keeps Moses' contrasting position and the full teaching commission with its practical purpose.
verses.before: But you, stand here with me, and I will speak to you all the commandment, the statutes, and the judgments that you will teach them, so that they may do them in the land that I am giving them to possess.’
verses.after: But you stay here with me. I will tell you the whole commandment, the statutes and rulings you are to teach them, so that they may practice them in the land I am giving them to possess.’
verses.tsw_comparator: But you, stand here with me, and I will speak to you all the commandment, the statutes, and the judgments that you shall teach them, so that they may do them in the land that I am giving them to possess.’

verses.rationale: Retains careful obedience and the road-direction image linking conduct to a path.
verses.before: So you will be careful to do just as the LORD your God commanded you. You will not turn aside to the right or to the left.
verses.after: So be careful to do what the LORD your God has commanded you. Do not turn aside to the right or to the left.
verses.tsw_comparator: So you shall be careful to do just as the LORD your God commanded you. You shall not turn aside to the right or to the left.

verses.rationale: Preserves walk and way, followed by all three stated benefits.
verses.before: In all the way that the LORD your God commanded you, you will walk, so that you may live, and it may go well with you, and you may prolong your days in the land that you will possess.
verses.after: Walk in the whole way the LORD your God has commanded you, so that you may live, it may go well with you, and you may remain long in the land you will possess.”
verses.tsw_comparator: In all the way that the LORD your God commanded you, you shall walk, so that you may live, and it may go well with you, and you may prolong your days in the land that you will possess.

verses.rationale: Keeps the singular commandment as the collective introduction and instruction aimed at practice.
verses.before: “And this is the commandment, the statutes, and the judgments that the LORD your God commanded me to teach you, to do in the land that you are crossing over to possess,
verses.after: “This is the commandment, the statutes and rulings the LORD your God commanded me to teach you, so that you may practice them in the land you are crossing over to possess.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And this is the commandment, the statutes, and the judgments that the LORD your God commanded me to teach you, to do in the land that you are crossing over to possess,

verses.rationale: Preserves the three named male generations, lifelong keeping, and the length-of-days purpose.
verses.before: so that you may fear the LORD your God, keeping all his statutes and his commandments that I command you—you, your child, and your child’s child—all the days of your life, and so that your days may be prolonged.
verses.after: Then you may fear the LORD your God, keeping all his statutes and commands that I give you—you, your son, and your grandson—all the days of your life, so that your days may be long.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that you may fear the LORD your God, keeping all his statutes and his commandments that I command you—you, your child, and your child’s child—all the days of your life, and so that your days may be prolonged.

verses.rationale: Retains hearing, doing, abundance, the land image, and the ancestral promise.
verses.before: Hear therefore, Israel, and be careful to do them, so that it may go well with you and so that you may multiply greatly, as the LORD, the God of your ancestors, spoke to you, in a land flowing with milk and honey.
verses.after: Hear, Israel, and be careful to do this, so that it may go well with you and you may become very numerous in a land flowing with milk and honey, as the LORD, the God of your fathers, promised you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hear therefore, Israel, and be careful to do them, so that it may go well with you and so that you may multiply greatly, as the LORD, the God of your ancestors, spoke to you, in a land flowing with milk and honey.

verses.rationale: Retains the one rendering of the compressed Hebrew and records the consequential LORD alone alternative in a note.
verses.before: Hear, Israel: The LORD is our God; the LORD is one.
verses.after: Hear, Israel: the LORD our God, the LORD is one.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hear, Israel: The LORD is our God; the LORD is one.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated all and the recognizable threefold total devotion without forcing artificial faculties.
verses.before: You will love the LORD your God with all your heart, with all your life, and with all your might.
verses.after: Love the LORD your God with all your heart, all your soul, and all your strength.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart, with all your life, and with all your might.

verses.rationale: Keeps words on the heart as the image preparing for repeated teaching.
verses.before: “These words that I command you today will be upon your heart.
verses.after: These words that I command you today must be on your heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: “These words that I command you today shall be upon your heart.

verses.rationale: Unfolds the intensive teaching verb as repetition and preserves the paired settings and daily actions.
verses.before: You will impress them upon your children and speak of them when you sit in your house, when you walk on the way, when you lie down, and when you rise.
verses.after: Teach them to your children again and again. Talk about them when you sit at home and when you walk along the road, when you lie down and when you get up.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall impress them upon your children and speak of them when you sit in your house, when you walk on the way, when you lie down, and when you rise.

verses.rationale: Retains the concrete binding instruction and anatomical placement; notes uncertainty about the rare term for bands.
verses.before: You will bind them as a sign on your hand, and they will be as frontlets between your eyes.
verses.after: Bind them as a sign on your hand, and let them be bands between your eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall bind them as a sign on your hand, and they shall be as frontlets between your eyes.

verses.rationale: Keeps both domestic doorposts and gates as distinct writing locations.
verses.before: You will write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates.
verses.after: Write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates.

verses.rationale: Retains the named ancestors and begins the sustained list of unearned abundance without collapsing it.
verses.before: “And when the LORD your God brings you into the land that he swore to your ancestors, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, to give you—great and good cities that you did not build,
verses.after: When the LORD your God brings you into the land he swore to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, to give you—a land with large, good towns you did not build,
verses.tsw_comparator: “And when the LORD your God brings you into the land that he swore to your ancestors, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, to give you—great and good cities that you did not build,

verses.rationale: Keeps each item and repeated did not, including the labor of hewing water storage.
verses.before: houses full of every good thing that you did not fill, cisterns hewn that you did not hew, vineyards and olive trees that you did not plant—and you eat and are satisfied,
verses.after: with houses full of good things you did not fill, hewn cisterns you did not hew, and vineyards and olive trees you did not plant—and you eat your fill,
verses.tsw_comparator: houses full of every good thing that you did not fill, cisterns hewn that you did not hew, vineyards and olive trees that you did not plant—and you eat and are satisfied,

verses.rationale: Completes the abundance warning with memory of enslavement and liberation.
verses.before: guard yourself, lest you forget the LORD who brought you out from the land of Egypt, from the house of slavery.
verses.after: be careful not to forget the LORD, who brought you out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
verses.tsw_comparator: guard yourself, lest you forget the LORD who brought you out from the land of Egypt, from the house of slavery.

verses.rationale: Retains fear, service, and the actual oath instruction without generalizing it into speech ethics.
verses.before: The LORD your God you will fear, him you will serve, and by his name you will swear.
verses.after: Fear the LORD your God, serve him, and swear by his name.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD your God you shall fear, him you shall serve, and by his name you shall swear.

verses.rationale: Keeps the local temptation and lets the causal explanation follow across the verse boundary.
verses.before: You will not go after other gods, from the gods of the peoples who are around you,
verses.after: Do not follow other gods, the gods of the peoples around you,
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not go after other gods, from the gods of the peoples who are around you,

verses.rationale: Preserves jealousy, burning anger, and threatened destruction without weakening the consequence.
verses.before: for the LORD your God in your midst is a jealous God, lest the anger of the LORD your God burn against you and he destroy you from the face of the ground.
verses.after: for the LORD your God among you is a jealous God. Otherwise the anger of the LORD your God will burn against you, and he will destroy you from the face of the ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: for the LORD your God in your midst is a jealous God, lest the anger of the LORD your God burn against you and he destroy you from the face of the ground.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated testing verb and the named event as the warning's anchor.
verses.before: “You will not test the LORD your God as you tested him at Massah.
verses.after: Do not put the LORD your God to the test as you tested him at Massah.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You shall not test the LORD your God as you tested him at Massah.

verses.rationale: Renders the emphatic keeping construction as diligence and retains the categories of instruction.
verses.before: You will diligently keep the commandments of the LORD your God, his testimonies, and his statutes that he commanded you.
verses.after: Be diligent in keeping the commands of the LORD your God, the testimonies and statutes he has commanded you.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall diligently keep the commandments of the LORD your God, his testimonies, and his statutes that he commanded you.

verses.rationale: Keeps right and good, the eyes idiom, and the purpose chain continuing into the next verse.
verses.before: You will do what is right and good in the eyes of the LORD, so that it may go well with you and you may enter and possess the good land that the LORD swore to your ancestors,
verses.after: Do what is right and good in the LORD's eyes, so that it may go well with you and you may enter and possess the good land the LORD swore to your fathers,
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall do what is right and good in the eyes of the LORD, so that it may go well with you and you may enter and possess the good land that the LORD swore to your ancestors,

verses.rationale: Preserves dispossession as part of the preceding purpose sequence without adding a new independent command.
verses.before: driving out all your enemies from before you, as the LORD has spoken.
verses.after: driving out all your enemies before you, as the LORD promised.
verses.tsw_comparator: driving out all your enemies from before you, as the LORD has spoken.

verses.rationale: Keeps the future son's question and its meaningful our God versus commanded you wording.
verses.before: “When your child asks you in time to come, saying, ‘What are the testimonies, statutes, and judgments that the LORD our God commanded you?’
verses.after: When your son asks you in days to come, ‘What do the testimonies, statutes, and rulings mean that the LORD our God commanded you?’
verses.tsw_comparator: “When your child asks you in time to come, saying, ‘What are the testimonies, statutes, and judgments that the LORD our God commanded you?’

verses.rationale: Preserves the intergenerational we of the reply, Pharaoh's ownership, and the divine strong hand.
verses.before: then you will say to your child, ‘We were Pharaoh’s servants in Egypt, but the LORD brought us out from Egypt with a strong hand.
verses.after: tell your son, ‘We were Pharaoh's slaves in Egypt, and the LORD brought us out of Egypt with a strong hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: then you shall say to your child, ‘We were Pharaoh’s servants in Egypt, but the LORD brought us out from Egypt with a strong hand.

verses.rationale: Keeps the destructive force of the wonders and all three named targets rather than treating them as merely impressive.
verses.before: The LORD gave signs and wonders, great and harmful, against Egypt, against Pharaoh and all his house, before our eyes.
verses.after: Before our eyes the LORD brought great and terrible signs and wonders on Egypt, Pharaoh, and his whole household.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD gave signs and wonders, great and harmful, against Egypt, against Pharaoh and all his house, before our eyes.

verses.rationale: Preserves the deliberate out-to-in movement and its connection with the land oath.
verses.before: He brought us out from there in order to bring us in, to give us the land that he swore to our ancestors.
verses.after: He brought us out of there to bring us in and give us the land he swore to our fathers.
verses.tsw_comparator: He brought us out from there in order to bring us in, to give us the land that he swore to our ancestors.

verses.rationale: Keeps practice and fear with both enduring welfare and present survival as their stated purpose.
verses.before: The LORD commanded us to do all these statutes, to fear the LORD our God, for our good all the days, to keep us alive, as it is this day.
verses.after: The LORD commanded us to practice all these statutes and to fear the LORD our God, for our good always and to keep us alive, as we are today.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD commanded us to do all these statutes, to fear the LORD our God, for our good all the days, to keep us alive, as it is this day.

verses.rationale: Retains righteousness and the conditional careful obedience without inserting a later doctrinal account of merit or salvation.
verses.before: And it will be righteousness for us if we are careful to do all this commandment before the LORD our God, as he commanded us.’
verses.after: It will be righteousness for us if we are careful to practice this whole commandment before the LORD our God, as he commanded us.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: And it will be righteousness for us if we are careful to do all this commandment before the LORD our God, as he commanded us.’
